newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Eletrobras sell-off to begin in '97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Eletrobras sell-off to begin in '97.

text.p: The privatization of state power firm Eletrobras' major assets will begin by the end of 1997 and minority shareholders will be able to swap their stake for shares in the privatized units, a government official said.

"By the end of 1997 some of Eletrobras major assets will be put up for sale. It is our intention to respect the interests of minority shareholders," Jose Pio Borges, Brazil's National Development Bank vice-president, said at a seminar on the electrical sector in Sao Paulo.

Borges said Eletrobras minority shareholders will have the right to decide whether to maintain their stakes in Eletrobras or swap them for some of the firms assets which will be privatized, such as hydroelectric plants and power distribution companies.
However, he noted the government has not yet defined the mechanism through which the shareholders will be able to swap their stake in Eletrobras for the privatized assets.
Currently, 24 percent of the firm's capital is publicly traded.

Borges also said the first part of the project for the restructuring of the electrical sector, which has been prepared by British consulting firm Coopers & Lybrant, is expected to be ready between November and December.

This first part, he said, will set rules for pricing Eletrobras assets. These rules will also regulate the selloff of Eletrobras' 11 small hydroelectric and thermoelectric plants slated for privatization early next year.
Eletrobras plans to raise 3 billion reais from the sale of these small power plants.
